result.note: Tests the new WPI series (base year, basket, weights), the reclassification of crude and gas, and the PPI suite with the old WPI's five-year sunset.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the new Wholesale Price Index (WPI) series that the Government of India announced in June 2026:
items: It uses 2022–23 as its base year.
The basket of tracked items shrinks from 957 to 697.
Item weights reflect domestic production rather than net trade.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the basket grows from 697 to 957 items, not the other way round. The new series replaces a 15-year-old yardstick, and its production-based weights give a more accurate picture of what India actually makes.
questions.source: Weights now reflect domestic production rather than net trade, giving a more accurate picture of what India actually makes.

questions.prompt: Under the new Wholesale Price Index series announced in June 2026, crude petroleum and gas have been moved into which group?
questions.explain: Crude petroleum and gas move from Primary Articles to Fuel and Power. Solar, wind and nuclear power also enter the energy group for the first time.
questions.source: Crude petroleum and gas migrate from "Primary Articles" to "Fuel and Power."

questions.prompt: In June 2026, India announced a new suite of Producer Price Indices (PPIs) alongside a revised WPI. Consider the following statements:
items: PPIs are the International Monetary Fund's preferred standard for measuring producer prices.
The PPI suite covers seven service sectors, including banking, telecom and aviation.
The old WPI series will be discontinued as soon as the new series is released.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong because the old WPI gets a five-year sunset before it is discontinued entirely. The US, EU and Japan had already moved from WPI-style indices to PPIs years ago.
questions.source: The old WPI gets a five-year sunset before it's discontinued entirely.
